Ouezon City http: /,'www dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 52 s. 2023 HON. VALENTIN C. ALONZO Vice Mayor Aroroy, Masbate Thru: MR. ROY C. GERONIMO Secretary to the Sanggunian Dear Vice Mayor Alonzo: This has reference to your letter dated April 17, 2023, requesting for the Department's clarification on the following: I. What is the distinction between a municipal resolution and a municipal ordinance? 2. Is Municipal Ordinance No. 026-A a municipal resolution or a municipal ordinance? 3. Assuming that Municipal Ordinance No. 026-A is an ordinance, is it valid in substance considering that under the Philippine Mining Act of 1995, it is the National government which regulates mining activities through the DENR? 4. Assuming that Municipal Ordinance No. 026-A is valid, who or what may repeal or amend it and how may it be repealed or amended? Per representation, Filminera Resources Corporation holds a Mineral Production Sharing Agreement (MPSA) which allows it to among others, conduct mineral operations in Aroroy, Masbate. Filminera has lodged an application for the amendment of its Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) in view of the proposed expansion of its mineral operations in "Blue Quartz" and "Old Lady" pits located in Barangay Capsay. In view thereof, Filminera has requested the Sangguniang Bayan of Aroroy, Masbate to endorse favorably its mining activities. However, the Sanggunian cannot act on the said request because of Municipal Ordinance No. 026-A, entitled "AN ORDINANCE DECLARING THE SANGGUNIANG BAYAN FIRM RESOLVE TO STRONGLY OPPOSE AT ANY TIME ANY FURTHER EXPANSION OF THE MINING OPERATIONS OF THE FILMINERA RESOURCES CORPORATION IN THIS MUNICIPALITY" Moreover, the Sanggunian is in quandary of the validity of the subject ordinance as it appears to be a mere declaration of the sentiment or opinion of the 8th Sanggunian. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Hence, the above stated queries In reply to your first query, the Supreme Court in the case of Municipality of Paranaque vs. V.M. Realty Corporation' has distinguished an ordinance from a resolution in this manner. "A municipal ordinance is different from a resolution. An ordinance is a law, but a resolution is merely a declaration of the sentiment or opinion on a lawmaking body on a specific matter. An ordinance possesses a general and permanent character, but a resolution is temporary in nature. Additionally, the two are enacted differently — a third reading is necessary for an ordinance, but not for a resolution, unless decided otherwise by majority of all the Sanggunian members. However, in the case of Favis vs. The City of Baguio City, et al.2, the Supreme Court held that even if the measure is denominated as a resolution if it is passed in the manner and with the statutory formality required in the enactment of an ordinance, it will be binding and effective as an ordinance. Thus, the answer to query number 2 is dependent on the manner it is passed. For query number 3, the main mining legislation in the country is RA No. 7942 or the Philippine Mining Act of 1995. We also have the Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 7942 and DENR issuances, which supplement said law. Section 8 of RA 7942 and Section 6, Chapter II of its IRR of RA 7942 state that the DENR "xxx is the primary Govemment agency responsible for the conservation, management, development and proper use of the State's mineral resources including those in reservations, watershed areas and lands of the public domain, " which therefore corroborate your view that it is national government which regulates mining activities through the DENR However, please be informed that the same IRR (Section 8) of RA 7942 also gives unto local government units several roles, to wit: "Section 8. Role of Local Government Subject to Section 8 of the Act and pursuant to the Local Government Code and other pertinent laws, the LGUs shall have the following roles in mining projects within their respective jurisdictions: a. To ensure that relevant laws on public notice, public consultation and public participation are complied with; b. In coordination with the Bureau/RegionaI Office(s) and subject to valid and existing mining rights, to approve applications for smallscale mining, sand and gravel, quarry, guano, gemstone gathering and gratuitous permits and for industrial sand and gravel permits not exceeding five (5) hectares; c. To receive their share as provided for by law in the wealth generated from the utilization of mineral resources and thus enhance economic progress and national development; 1 G.R. d. To facilitate the process by which the community shall reach an informed decision on the social acceptability of a mining project as a requirement for securing an ECC, e. To participate in the monitoring of any tilining activity as a member of the Multipartite Monitoring Teanl refened to in Section 185 hereof, as provided for in Sections 182 to 187 hereof, g. To be the recipient of social inflastrtlc,ture and comrnunity development projects for the utilization of the host and neighboring communities in accordance with Chapter XIV heteof. h To act as tnediator between the ICCs and the Contractor(s) as may be requested. To coordinate with the Department and Bureau in the implementation of the Act and these implennenting rules and regulations in their respective jurisdictions. In areas covered by the Southern Philippines Council for Peace and Development, Autonotnous Region of Muslim Mindanao and future similar units, the appropriate offices of said units shall coordinate with the Department and Bureau in the implementation of the Act and these implementing rules and regulations; and j To perform such other powers and functions as may be provided for by applicable laws, rules and regulations. Further, Section 2 of EO No. 79, series of 20123, provides. "SECTION 2. Full Enforcement of Environmental Standards in Mining. The Government in general, and the Department of Environmental and Natural Resources (DENR) in particular, in coordination with concerned LGUs, shall ensure that environmental standards in mining, as prescribed by the various mining and environmental laws, rules, and regulations, shall be fully and strictly enforced, and appropriate sanctions meted out against violators thereof. In line with the above, only those who are able to strictly comply with all the pertinent requirements shall be eligible for the grant of mining rights, pursuant to the applicable provisions of RA No. 7942." Based on the foregoing, while the DENR is the primary agency responsible for the conservation, management, development and proper use of the State's mineral resources, our policies also acknowledge the roles of the concerned LGUs. It may also be prudent to emphasize that while this Department exercises general supervision over local government units (LGUs), we have no authority to declare invalid any ordinance duly enacted by the sanggunian. Only the courts have the authority to do so upon initiation of the appropriate action mentioned above. Moreover, the Department is proscribed to act on queries regarding presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar cases. For the last query, an ordinance may be amended or repealed only by another ordinance, enacted with the same formalities as the ordinance being amended or repealed4. In the event that the sanggunian opted to amend the subject ordinance, the Entitled "INSTITUTIONALIZING AND IMPLEMENTING REFORMS IN THE PHILIPPINE MINING SECTOR PROVIDING POLICIES AND GUIDELINES TO ENSURE ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND RESPONSIBLE MINING IN THE UTILIZATION OF MINERAL RESOURCES" 4 DILG Opinion No. 105, s. 2022 dated September 28, 2022 Page 3 of 4

sanggunian shall consider Chapter V15 of DENR Administrative Order No. 2010-21 or the Revised Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 7942 or the Philippine Mining Act of 1995 — providing therein, among others, the eligibility of applicant for mineral and maxinwm areas allowed under a mineral agreement. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you.
